newsitem.title: USA: Anadarko sees 1997 output up 17 percent.
newsitem.headline: Anadarko sees 1997 output up 17 percent.

text.p: Anadarko Petroleum Corp estimates that it can increase production oil and natural gas 17 percent this year from the 1996 level to 44 million barrels of oil equivalent.

The company said in a statement with second-quarter earnings that natural gas production in the first six months of 1997 was 86.1 billion cubic feet and that crude oil and condensate volumes increased 26 percent to 4.3 million barrels.
The increase in 1997 production will come from 500 wells in a dozen fields
"We are not exhausting a finite set of resources - the more we shoot and the more we drill, the more opportunities we see," said Robert Allison, Anadarko's chief executive.
"By themselves, the Sudden Impact projects are not large by Wall Street standards, but the effect of investing over $300 million on development projects is significant to Anadarko," he said.
In the first half, appraisal of investments showed an expected rate of return above 40 percent, he added. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
